## Nexus 1.1.4

This release is the accumulated work of builds 42–54. Nothing here changes where your tabs, accounts or
settings live — the installer upgrades in place, and if you already run Nexus it will offer this update
by itself (8 seconds after launch, and every 15 minutes after that).

### The AI view stops going blank

The bug behind most of this release. Several separate faults could leave a tab showing nothing:

- the view came back blank after the window was resumed, minimised or covered by a panel;
- the view was left hidden while the app believed it was on screen;
- a panel could be left open behind a hidden view, eating every keystroke;
- and a tab that had already been rebuilt three times was refused a fourth rebuild **for the rest of the
  session**, so closing and reopening it did not help.

All four are fixed. A view is now verified on screen, a wedged view rebuilds itself, and a page is only
re-hidden when the check finds something wrong — tab switching never waits for it.

### A black page is no longer mistaken for a healthy one

A page painted into its own background was reported as "painted": the frame had content in it, it was just
unreadable. Nexus now measures how dark the frame actually is, asks the page for its own computed colours,
and — when its text and background have collapsed into each other — re-applies the stylesheet for that
view with text it can show. No reload, no eviction.

### The diagnostics can name the cause

The export now carries, for every tab: the last verdict for that view, when it was taken, the frame's
brightness, the page's own background and text colours, how many bad frames and rebuilds it has had, which
stylesheet is on it, and what is painted down the sidebar's right edge. If something goes wrong again, the
export will say which kind of wrong it was instead of needing a screenshot.

### Less CPU for the same app

- the status observer injected into every AI page no longer forces a layout pass hundreds of times a
  second;
- the shell stops animating after 15 seconds without input;
- the CPU figures in the diagnostics are now measured per process and per view, so the next report can say
  where the cost is instead of rounding it.

### Uploading a folder

- **Windows:** a folder now lists as its folders, foldable at each level, instead of one flat row of
  `folder\file.py` names — and the paths written into the bundle use `/`, which every tool downstream
  understands.
- **Part size is now on the upload popup**, next to Upload: 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 MB, with a live estimate
  of how many parts your selection will arrive as. It is remembered between uploads and launches, and it is
  the size the upload actually uses (until now the control only affected the preview).

### Notifications, tabs and colours

- a notification can no longer cost the page its frame, and it says what the in-app card says — once;
- a notification names the tab it came from;
- a restored tab comes back pinned, in its place, and coloured on the first frame;
- every tab row wears its provider's colour, at the intensity you chose, not just the active one.

### Linux

The release now ships an **AppImage** alongside the pacman package, and the update feed is verified as part
of the release. Linux users on AppImage get automatic updates for the first time.

### Checks

`npm run typecheck` clean, full suite green (2,191 tests), and the release itself refuses to publish if the
tag, the version, or the update feed files disagree.
